content: Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) encompasses a broad range of liver conditions, starting from simple fat accumulation in the liver (steatosis) to more severe forms, such as Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis (NASH) and cirrhosis. These advanced stages can progress to hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer). NAFLD is particularly common among adults with type 2 diabetes, highlighting a significant overlap between metabolic dysfunction and liver disease. NASH, the progressive and more severe form of NAFLD, is one of the leading causes of liver transplantation globally, underscoring its clinical significance. Management of NAFLD in individuals with diabetes necessitates targeted therapeutic strategies, given the strong association of this condition with increased cardiovascular and metabolic risks.
